title: NimblePulse weekly prefetch + cache tuning sync
summary: Weekly POC sync to review prefix/KV hit rates, discuss prompt reuse strategies, tune prefetch window and eviction TTLs, and align on next steps for a canary run. Customer is leaning toward Redwood Dedicated if hit rates and latency targets improve; security docs requested for Private deployment evaluation.
next_steps: Redwood to send tuned config + benchmark script
Customer to share two weeks of anonymized prompt traces
Schedule 6-hour canary on staging next Wed
Security team to review SOC2/KMS docs and confirm access model
action_items: Maya Chen | send pilot config (prefetch=3, eviction_ttl=600s) + benchmark harness | 2027-09-16
Diego Alvarez | run KV mapping sweep and upload heatmap CSV to shared drive | 2027-09-17
Liam O'Connor | produce anonymized prompt flow dump (2 weeks) | 2027-09-18
Sofia Rhee | validate KMS roles and VPC peering checklist for Private eval | 2027-09-20
transcript:
[15:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for hopping on, we got about 42 minutes so we'll go through the numbers quickly and then dive into tuning.
[15:12] Liam O'Connor: Thanks Maya, excited to see the hit rate changes from last week, we've been seeing some variance in the afternoon spikes.
[15:20] Diego Alvarez: Quick note, I pulled the 24-hour traces — the prefix hit went from about 18% up to 34% after the template normalization we applied, KV hit moved 41% to 55% in the high reuse cohort, overall tokens saved ~8%. Some of the telemetry is noisy during brownouts.
[15:45] Marcus Lee: Wait 8% tokens saved sounds low vs what we'd hoped. Can you break down by route?
[15:52] Diego Alvarez: Sure, route /generate-chat accounts for most traffic — prefix reuse there is higher, ~42% during morning; lower on /summary where prompts are varied. The prefetch window we used was 2 prior prompts, that looks like it's underfetching on multi-turn flows.
[16:18] Maya Chen: So proposed change is prefetch window -> 3 (include 3 prior messages) and bump eviction TTL from 300s -> 600s for sessions that show high reuse. That should increase effective prefix hit for long sessions.
[16:36] Ava Kim: Curious about memory/cost tradeoffs, doubling TTL could increase KV memory usage — what's the ballpark?
[16:43] Priya Patel: Good question — on our Dedicated clusters we've seen memory increase ~12-18% for those sessions; with eviction heuristics we can cap growth by cohort. We also proposed adaptive eviction where TTL is extended only if observed reuse > 35% in the last N requests.
[17:05] Liam O'Connor: Adaptive sounds good, but we also need to preserve 95th percentile latency under 220ms. Last week had a tail at 310ms during the 10:30 UTC spike.
[17:14] Diego Alvarez: Right, that spike correlates with large batch consolidation and a heavy KV lookups for long contexts. We can change routing policy so large-context requests go to nodes with higher memory headroom and fall back to a smaller quantized model if under pressure.
[17:36] Sofia Rhee: For Private deployment we'll need audit logs and KMS integration — Marcus, are you comfortable with the on-prem cert model?
[17:45] Marcus Lee: We'll review but yes, KMS is must-have; we can't bring plaintext keys into the cluster. Also need SSO + RBAC.
[17:53] Maya Chen: We'll attach SOC2 + KMS integration guide in the follow-up. Diego, can you note any additional infra asks?
[17:59] Diego Alvarez: We'll need an IAM service account in their staging VPC and a minimal peering setup. Also we'll recommend enabling prefix-level telemetry with sampling at 10% to avoid egress costs.
[18:20] Liam O'Connor: On the prompt reuse side— we ran a small experiment normalizing template variable names and grouping semantically identical prompts. That alone bumped prefix reuse on FAQ-type queries from 23% to 48%.
[18:35] Maya Chen: Nice, that suggests a short-term playbook: 1) normalize templates 2) apply prefetch=3 3) adaptive eviction TTL. Combined should move us into the 50-65% hit rate band for high-cohort traffic.
[18:50] Ava Kim: Are there risks to hallucination with more aggressive reuse?
[18:56] Priya Patel: Minimal — reuse only affects prefix caching not response sampling; we do watch for stale context. For safety, we add a prefix validation step: when we reuse a cached prefix, compute a lightweight signature and if mismatch above threshold we redraw. It's cheap and reduces stale-context errors.
[19:20] Diego Alvarez: Also to reduce cost we think a hybrid prefetch: short TTL for low-reuse cohorts and extended TTL for identified high-reuse cohorts. That requires cohorting logic which we've sketched in the config.
[19:38] Liam O'Connor: Can you share that config? We want to test locally first.
[19:42] Maya Chen: Yes I'll send a YAML for canary. Diego will include the heatmap and telemetry script.
[19:50] Marcus Lee: On the SLA/commit side — if we do Dedicated, what are guaranteed hit rates or latencies?
[19:57] Maya Chen: We don't lock absolute hit rates (they depend on app behavior) but Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower tail latency, and we can size pools to meet your 95th percentile target. We'll include SLO guidance in the proposal.
[20:12] Sofia Rhee: For the canary, what's the proposed duration and traffic slice?
[20:18] Diego Alvarez: We recommend a 6-hour staging canary with 10% of production-like traffic routed through our prefetch path, then a 24-hour extended run if metrics look good. Bake metrics: prefix/KV hit rate, tokens saved, 95/99 latency, error rate.
[20:40] Ava Kim: Will Redwood's console show token-level cost breakdown per route?
[20:44] Priya Patel: Yes, Console gives per-route token, latency, and cost. We'll attach a short explainer gif in the follow-up.
[20:56] Liam O'Connor: A few clarifying questions: 1) sampling rate for prefix telemetry — you said 10% is safe; 2) what about model quantization fallback — how fast is a fallback?
[21:08] Diego Alvarez: Sampling 10% is our default; you can adjust. Quantized fallback takes ~120-200ms additional warmup for KV cache depending on sequence length but is intended as graceful degradation.
[21:25] Marcus Lee: Any impact to throughput if many sessions get extended TTL?
[21:30] Priya Patel: We'll use cohort caps; also session affinity helps so hot sessions stay on nodes with headroom. Without caps throughput can degrade but our autoscaler plus routing mitigates it.
[21:50] Maya Chen: OK let's recap — today we agreed to push prefetch window to 3, set eviction_ttl=600s for high-reuse cohort, enable adaptive TTL rule, and run a 6-hour canary next Wed. Action items are in the notes.
[22:08] Liam O'Connor: One more ask — can you provide a short list of what changes we should make to our prompt templates to maximize reuse?
[22:15] Diego Alvarez: Yes — make variable placeholders explicit, avoid free-form salutations in prompts, canonicalize timestamps, and group instructions before dynamic content. We'll attach a 1-pager.
[22:33] Ava Kim: Great, that helps. Any blockers on Redwood side?
[22:38] Maya Chen: Nothing blocking. We'll send the config and security docs by Friday.
[22:45] Marcus Lee: Thanks all, we'll prioritize the prompt dump and KMS verification.
[22:50] Maya Chen: Thanks team, we'll follow up in email with links and scheduling for the canary.
[22:58] [meeting ends]

Notes on quality: automated transcript mis-heard a few product names (e.g., 'K-V cash' instead of KV cache) and some speaker labels may be off in overlapping talk.
